bull_argument.argument:
Meta's impression growth of 14% and ad-pricing growth of 12% underpin 28% revenue growth, demonstrating monetisation rather than hypothetical AI demand. H1 FCF remains positive at $13.170bn and cash/securities total $90.260bn. A plausible buy case is that this growing cash-producing franchise earns better returns on infrastructure and translates its revenue momentum into recovering owner cash.

This requires improvement: Q2 FCF was only $784m, H1 FCF declined 30.3%, and operating margin remains lower even after illustrative legal/severance addbacks. Long-term debt of $83.664bn and separate operating leases prevent a simplistic net-cash claim. The estimated 21.17x forward multiple offers potential compensation if cash conversion recovers, not proof that it will. Slowing price momentum favors monitoring actual capex productivity before assuming the investment surge is temporary.
key_points: Observed ad-volume and pricing growth support the recurring franchise.
Positive H1 FCF provides a base for recovery despite quarterly compression.
Lease exposure, margin erosion and capex returns determine per-share upside.

bear_argument.argument:
Meta's ad growth and positive $13.170bn H1 FCF preserve operating merit, but H1 cash fell 30.3% and Q2 FCF was only $784m. Adding back identified legal and severance charges produces an illustrative 36.77% operating margin, still below 43%; compression is therefore not entirely explained by those charges.

Capex guidance of $130–145bn requires continuing demand and productive infrastructure returns. Cash/securities of $90.260bn versus $83.664bn long-term debt excludes $26.229bn noncurrent operating leases. The bull's 21.17x forward multiple offers conditional earnings participation, but cash conversion already worsened and recurring costs cannot simply be assumed away. Slowing momentum adds caution. The strongest reason to wait is observed investment and margin pressure, not a requirement for certainty about every future capex dollar.
key_points: H1 FCF fell 30.3% despite revenue growth.
Illustrative charge-adjusted margin remains below prior year.
Capex and lease obligations qualify funding cushion.
bear_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: The bull's monetisation engine is real, but improved owner cash is still prospective. Even illustrative charge addbacks leave margin at 36.77% versus 43%, and the measured 30.3% H1 FCF decline cannot be dismissed as temporary without evidence.

bull_argument.argument:
The bear correctly shows that even illustrative charge removal leaves margin below the prior 43%; the recovery cannot be explained solely by exceptional costs. The counterweight is a franchise producing $64.088bn H1 CFO while impression and pricing growth jointly drove 28% revenue growth. Investment consumes much of that cash, but the underlying monetisation engine is generating funds rather than relying only on financing.

H1 FCF of $13.170bn remains positive after the specified cash investments and finance-lease principal, although it declined materially. The purchase scenario is greater cash productivity from the expanding infrastructure, at a conditional 21.17x forward earnings basis. It does not assume legal costs vanish or lease obligations are covered by a simplistic net-cash figure. Current pressure favors measured conviction, but positive cash and growing demand preserve recovery upside.
key_points: H1 CFO identifies a substantial internal funding engine.
Margin remains compressed even after illustrative charge adjustments.
Cash-productivity recovery is the upside scenario, not a completed fact.
bull_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: I accept 36.77% remains below 43% and FCF fell30.3%. The narrower rebuttal is $64.088bn H1 CFO and still-positive $13.170bn FCF show an internally cash-producing franchise. Productive investment could recover owner cash, but its probability is not established by addbacks or forecast P/E.

bear_argument.argument:
The bull's $64.088bn H1 CFO and $13.170bn FCF establish a cash-producing franchise despite infrastructure demands. This answers any implication that expansion depends only on external financing. The current counterexample remains specific: H1 FCF declined 30.3%, Q2 was only $784m, and illustrative charge-adjusted operating margin of 36.77% still trails 43%.

Capex guidance of $130–145bn raises the hurdle for monetisation to become owner cash. The $26.229bn noncurrent operating leases cannot disappear from funding analysis, and legal costs cannot simply be assumed nonrecurring. At 21.17x forecast earnings, recovery could reward ownership, but requires improved productivity while current cash and margins worsen. The bull answers business viability; it does not offset that measured deterioration sufficiently to support an aggressive recovery purchase on revenue growth alone.
key_points: Positive CFO and FCF support business viability.
Cash and adjusted operating margins are already deteriorating.
Forward valuation needs recovery amid heavy capex and leases.
bear_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: The bull correctly acknowledges current pressure and preserves upside from monetisation. It has not answered the decline in cash or residual margin compression; these observed costs, rather than uncertain perfection, justify restraint.

bull_case_summary: Meta has $64.088bn H1 CFO and still-positive $13.170bn FCF alongside strong ad monetisation. Round two accepts residual margin compression after charge addbacks and defends conditional recovery from an internally cash-producing franchise.
bear_case_summary: The bear accepts viability but stresses H1 FCF down 30.3%, only $784m Q2 FCF and illustrative adjusted margin of 36.77% below 43%. Heavy capex guidance and separate leases make a 21.17x forecast multiple depend on actual cash-productivity recovery.
key_points_of_agreement: Demand and positive cash support a real franchise.
Compression is not explained entirely by identified charges.
Legal costs and leases cannot be assumed away.
key_points_of_disagreement: Whether monetisation and internal cash sufficiently compensate current conversion deterioration for a recovery purchase.
unresolved_uncertainties: Incremental infrastructure productivity and recurring legal costs.
Cash recovery under $130–145bn capex guidance and sustainable margins.
